newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sells one mln tonnes wheat to India.
newsitem.headline: Australia sells one mln tonnes wheat to India.

text.p: Australian Trade Minister Tim Fischer said on Friday the Australian Wheat Board has sold one million tonnes of Australian wheat to India.
"Today it will be announced that the Australian Wheat Board has sold an additional million tonnes of wheat to India, making a total of 2.3 million tonnes (this year)," Fischer told reporters.
The Indian sale would be filled from the next harvest as well as the current bumber crop, Fischer said.
"On top of that, Pakistan has bought half a million tonnes of wheat."
Some of the Indian delivery was already underway from previous 1.3 million tonne sale, Fischer said.
"And the price is right, too, I might add," he said.
The sale was worth millions of Australian dollars, he said.
Nigel Officer, general manager international of the Australian Wheat Board (AWB), told Reuters he was "very pleased with the price".
He would not reveal a price beyond saying Australian wheat sales to India this year were worth about A$500 million.
The price in the latest deal was very reflective of the world market, which presently was fairly strong, he said. The price was also very supportive of the AWB pool price, he said.
Delivery in the Indian contract was July/August for 250,000 tonnes and November/December for the balance of 750,000 tonnes, from new crop, he said.
"We have never ever sold new crop wheat as far forward as this time," he said.
India was looking to rebuild buffer stocks and had concerns about the general crop situation but was largely replenishing stocks, he said.
India had not been expected to be in the market this year and certainly not at this sort of volume, he said.
"For us to sell 2.3 million tonnes to India certainly has come as a significant bonus. It's a windfall of A$500 million," he said.
Prices in Australia's sale to Pakistan, which was for April shipment, were about the same as the Indian deal, he said.
